title: Improving Short- and Long-Term Type 2 Diabetes Risk Prediction for Middle-Aged British Adults
source: User-supplied publisher PDF; local extracted.md; publisher supplementary DOCX; cached fulltext XML and verified metadata
contribution: Develops baseline clinical Cox tools for 5-, 10- and 15-year incident diabetes risk with WHII development and ELSA evaluation, comparing predictor selectors and presenting scores, groups and nomograms.
method: Complete-case cohort; 70/30 WHII split; LASSO-Cox 10-fold/one-SE plus bootstrap stability, RSF permutation-vs-noise selection and best subset/AIC; all final models Cox; calibration, DCA and MICE sensitivity.
best_metric: No single best model claimed. Table 2 p10579: ELSA 5-year C-index 0.878 (95% CI 0.844-0.908), LASSO-selected Cox; RSF-selected Cox 0.876 (0.843-0.908). These differ from continuous risk-score C-indices 0.800/0.801 in section 3.3.1 p10580.
vs_baseline: Within the same cohorts/horizons the three Cox predictor sets had broadly similar performance. Do not numerically rank against QDiabetes across different cohorts. Same-layer dinh2019_data_driven_nhanes is cross-sectional label classification and not a longitudinal metric comparator.
gap: Test/external-informed tool selection; complete-case selection; ELSA self-report; no competing risks; incomplete PH, code and external-calibration verification.
verdict_reason: Useful evidence and teaching reference for baseline prognosis with explicit limits; not a confirmed reproduction candidate or clinically validated implementation.

claim_provenance.claim: All three final candidate prediction models were Cox regression models, using predictor sets selected by LASSO-Cox, random survival forests or best subset selection.
WHII Phase 3 (1991-1994) was baseline and follow-up ended by Phase 9 (2007-2009); ELSA used Wave 2 (2004-2005) to Wave 10 (2021-2023).
The WHII analytic sample contained 6431 people: 4502 training and 1929 test participants.

location.section: 3.1.1 Characteristics of Included Participants in WHII

claim_provenance.claim: WHII had 547 training and 235 test diabetes events; median follow-up was 16.1 years in both sets.
The ELSA analytic sample contained 2190 participants, 255 incident diabetes cases and median follow-up of 14.2 years.

location.section: 3.2.1 Characteristics of Included Participants in External ELSA Dataset

claim_provenance.claim: LASSO used 10-fold cross-validation with a one-standard-error penalty choice, 1000 training-set bootstrap samples and a >=70% inclusion threshold.
The LASSO, RSF and best-subset procedures selected 9, 13 and 12 conceptual predictors respectively.
In ELSA at 5 years, time-dependent C-indices were 0.878 (95% CI 0.844-0.908) for LASSO-selected Cox, 0.876 (0.843-0.908) for RSF-selected Cox and 0.867 (0.829-0.902) for best-subset-selected Cox.
In ELSA at 10 years, C-indices were 0.820 (0.786-0.849), 0.822 (0.790-0.851) and 0.808 (0.773-0.839) for LASSO-, RSF- and best-subset-selected Cox respectively.
ELSA continuous risk-score C-indices were 0.800 (0.773-0.827) for LASSO and 0.801 (0.774-0.827) for RSF; risk-group C-indices were 0.737 (0.715-0.759) and 0.727 (0.707-0.748).
WHII Test calibration slopes were 0.968 (0.857-1.079), 0.986 (0.872-1.100) and 0.896 (0.791-1.002) for LASSO-, RSF- and best-subset-selected models.
WHII Test five-year O/E ratios were 0.866 (0.537-1.218), 0.857 (0.530-1.248) and 0.852 (0.530-1.194) for LASSO-, RSF- and best-subset-selected models.
DCA thresholds of 25%, 50% and 75% were prespecified for comparison because universally accepted intervention or screening thresholds were unavailable for the examined horizons.
At the ELSA 15-year 25% threshold, reported net benefits were 0.026, 0.023 and 0.021 for RSF-, LASSO- and best-subset-selected models.
Candidate performance in WHII Test and ELSA informed selection of the primary prediction tools; the authors acknowledged selection-induced optimism.
The RSF-selected Cox model had VIF values of 15.24 for TyG and 13.12 for TG.

location.section: 3.3 Transforming Models Into Prediction Tools; Supplement Table S14

claim_provenance.claim: The primary analysis used complete cases; Table S2 reports exclusion of 1057 (14.1%) of 7488 participants for missing at least one candidate predictor.

MICE sensitivity analysis generated 20 WHII datasets, included predictor variables, follow-up time and event status, pooled coefficients using Rubin rules and evaluated risk scores externally in ELSA.
After WHII imputation, ELSA risk-score C-indices were 0.798 (0.771-0.826) and 0.799 (0.772-0.826) for LASSO- and RSF-selected models.
The authors acknowledged self-reported diabetes in ELSA, possible complete-case selection bias and absence of competing-risk analysis.
WHII and ELSA supporting data were not publicly available according to the paper and could be accessed on application to their respective custodians.
The tool has already been demonstrated to reduce diabetes incidence when implemented in clinical care.
RSF was the final prediction model and was shown to outperform Cox.
Including baseline fasting glucose necessarily leaks the future incident-diabetes label.

validation_caveat: External-source, selection-influenced evaluation; no confirmed untouched final test for the selected tools.
